name: manual_8c587f
claim: When a storage contract changes (here, receivers keep exact bytes), revisit every consumer that predicts stored sizes or hashes. The peer duplicate check must accept the exact UTF-8 size as well as the legacy LF and CRLF sizes, and still require authenticated SHA-256 content verification after the size gate.

decisions.notes: 2026-11-04: once peer receivers stored exact bytes, the outbox duplicate check still accepted only the all-LF and all-CRLF sizes, so a queued body with mixed line endings could never match its byte-exact remote copy and stayed queued as a name collision.
